tests.name: test_signed_area_of_a_ccw_square_is_positive_one
tests.what: Shoelace area of a CCW unit square is +1.

tests.name: test_signed_area_flips_with_winding
tests.what: Reversing vertex order negates the signed area (the orientation convention that face/zone direction logic depends on).

tests.name: test_signed_area_ignores_an_explicit_closing_vertex
tests.what: Repeating the first vertex at the end does not change the area.

tests.name: test_signed_area_of_a_triangle
tests.what: Area of a 3-4-5 right triangle is 6.
tests.concern: Three separate one-line analytic-area tests (square, triangle, L) are the same check on different shapes.

tests.name: test_signed_area_of_a_concave_polygon
tests.what: Area of an L-shaped concave hexagon is 3.
tests.concern: Same check as the square and triangle tests, on another shape.

tests.name: test_signed_area_of_a_degenerate_polygon_is_zero
tests.what: A 2-vertex polygon and an empty array both have area exactly 0.0.

tests.name: test_point_in_polygon_interior_and_exterior
tests.what: Basic inside/outside classification on the unit square.

tests.name: test_point_in_polygon_on_edge_and_on_vertex_count_as_inside
tests.what: Boundary points (on an edge or a vertex) count as inside; this is the documented inclusive policy that zone classification relies on.
tests.concern: This pins a policy choice (an inclusive boundary). The docstring says bridge-on-boundary classification needs it, so it is a real contract.

tests.name: test_point_in_polygon_respects_the_concavity
tests.what: A point in the bitten-out corner of the L is outside; one in the arm is inside.
tests.concern: Fully contained in test_point_in_polygon_is_winding_independent, which asserts the same two points on CONCAVE plus its reverse.

tests.name: test_point_in_polygon_is_winding_independent
tests.what: Concave containment gives the same answer for either winding.

tests.name: test_point_in_polygon_accepts_an_explicitly_closed_ring
tests.what: A ring whose first vertex is repeated at the end classifies the same as the open ring.

tests.name: test_point_in_polygon_of_a_degenerate_polygon_is_false
tests.what: A 2-vertex 'polygon' contains nothing, not even its own vertex.

tests.name: test_polyline_midpoint_is_the_middle_node
tests.what: polyline_midpoint returns the index-middle vertex, not the arc-length midpoint; this is documented as deliberate so the point lies exactly on the curve.
tests.concern: This pins a deliberate design choice (the middle node) that the source docstring justifies. It would only break if that choice were reversed.

tests.name: test_polyline_midpoint_of_an_empty_polyline_is_none
tests.what: An empty polyline gives None.

tests.name: test_polyline_midpoint_returns_a_copy_not_a_view
tests.what: The returned point is a writable copy, so writing to it neither raises nor corrupts a read-only memoised source array.

tests.name: test_interior_point_is_inside[x4: square, triangle, L, crescent]
tests.what: polygon_interior_point returns a point strictly classified inside, for convex, concave and crescent shapes.

tests.name: test_interior_point_is_winding_independent
tests.what: The interior point is inside for both windings of the L and the crescent.
tests.concern: The forward-winding half repeats the parametrized test; only the reversed polygons are new.

tests.name: test_interior_point_beats_the_vertex_mean_on_a_crescent
tests.what: Checks that the crescent fixture is a meaningful case (its vertex mean is outside) and that the interior point is inside it.
tests.concern: Its second assertion duplicates the crescent case of test_interior_point_is_inside. The first assertion only checks that the fixture is non-trivial, which is worth keeping as a guard on the fixture.

tests.name: test_interior_point_of_a_degenerate_polygon_is_none
tests.what: A 2-vertex polygon and a horizontal sliver (only one distinct y) give None.
tests.concern: The sliver case partly reflects the scanline implementation (one distinct ordinate means no scanline). It is still a reasonable contract: a degenerate polygon has no interior.

tests.name: test_arc_polyline_clips_to_the_cdist_window
tests.what: arc_polyline over [cdist[2], cdist[8]] of a grown manifold returns exactly nodes 2..8 (7 rows) with matching endpoints.
tests.concern: `len(arc) == 7` pins the inclusive-endpoints-at-node-cdists behaviour. Interpolating clipped endpoints, or treating the window ends exclusively, would break it while still being correct clipping. The tangle fixture is also heavier than this needs: a synthetic manifold would do.
tests.question: Is it a contract that arc_polyline includes the window endpoints exactly when they coincide with node cdists (no interpolation)?

tests.name: test_arc_polyline_reverse_flips_the_order
tests.what: reverse=True returns the forward polyline reversed.

tests.name: test_arc_polyline_on_an_empty_window_is_empty
tests.what: A cdist window entirely below 0 gives an empty polyline.

tests.name: test_oriented_bridge_polyline_runs_in_the_dynamical_direction
tests.what: For every bridge, the oriented polyline is the stored points or their reverse, and the bridge nodes' cdists are monotone.
tests.concern: Weak. It never checks that poly starts at low cdist (it accepts either orientation). The cdist check runs on the raw nodes, flipped if needed, not on poly, so it is really a bridge monotonicity check that test_growth_integration::test_bridges_individually_satisfy_invariants already covers. It also silently skips when poly is None.

tests.name: test_oriented_bridge_polyline_refuses_equal_cdist_endpoints
tests.what: Equal endpoint cdists (no orientation possible) give None.
tests.concern: Builds a full tangle with bridges just to get one bridge object.

tests.name: test_map_batch_detects_and_matches_loop
tests.what: map_batch on a batch-capable map matches the per-point loop, keeps the shape, and sets the private _map_batchable flag to True.
tests.concern: Asserts the private attribute `_map_batchable`. The equivalence and shape checks are the contract; the flag is an implementation detail of the detection.

tests.name: test_scalar_only_map_falls_back
tests.what: A scalar-only map still works through map_batch (per-point fallback), and _map_batchable is False.
tests.concern: Private `_map_batchable` assertion. Checking that a scalar-only map does not raise and matches the loop is enough.

tests.name: test_batch_and_fallback_growth_agree
tests.what: Growing 5 unstable iterations with a batch map and with a scalar-only map gives identical cdists and points; also asserts the private flag through wb._man_machine.system.
tests.concern: Reaches through two private attributes (`_man_machine.system._map_batchable`). The end-to-end equivalence is valuable and cheap. The flag asserts duplicate the two unit tests above.

tests.name: test_refinement_essentially_converges_to_cutoff
tests.what: After growth, fewer than 2% of consecutive pairs have curvature area >= area_cutoff, and none exceed it by 5x or more.
tests.concern: The 2%/5x thresholds are empirical tolerances, not derived ones. It calls the private `_curvature_area` and `_man_machine`, and it sits in the batched-map file although it tests the refiner.
tests.question: Is 'refinement leaves pairs below area_cutoff (with small slack)' a guarantee you want enforced, or only a diagnostic? Should it move to a refinement-focused file?

tests.name: test_parabolic_fit_matches_vandermonde[x5 seeds]
tests.what: The private closed-form _parabolic_fit matches a reference Vandermonde solve on 5 random well-conditioned triples.
tests.concern: This is an equivalence check for a past optimisation, on a private static method. It is cheap and the reference is mathematically defined (the unique parabola through 3 points), so it is fine as an oracle test. Five seeds add nothing over one or two.

tests.name: test_curvature_area_batch_matches_scalar
tests.what: The vectorized _curvature_area_batch equals the scalar _curvature_area on every consecutive pair of a grown manifold.
tests.concern: This compares two private implementations. It is useful as long as both paths exist; if the scalar path is removed as dead code, delete the test. It re-implements the neighbour walk by hand.
tests.question: Is the scalar _curvature_area still used in production, or only kept as a reference? If it is only a reference, this test pins dead code.

tests.name: test_enable_gpu_without_cupy_raises_clearly
tests.what: enable_gpu raises ImportError mentioning 'CuPy' when cupy cannot be imported; it skips when cupy is installed (as on this machine).
tests.concern: It never runs on this dev machine (CuPy is installed), so it is effectively dead locally. It could be made unconditional by monkeypatching the cupy import to fail.

tests.name: test_gpu_growth_matches_cpu
tests.what: Growth with enable_gpu(min_batch_points=1) gives the same unstable cdists as the CPU path.
tests.concern: The GPU build hardcodes the guess [4, -4] where the CPU build uses saddle_guesses, so it duplicates the setup logic slightly differently. It compares cdists only, not points.

tests.name: test_refined_cdist_is_mean_of_neighbours
tests.what: The private _get_refined_point gives the new point the arithmetic mean of its neighbours' cdists.
tests.concern: Its own docstring says it is a characterization test, not a correctness gate: the mean rule is 'itself suspect' and may change. It enforces a rule the author does not endorse, via a private method.
tests.question: Is the mean-of-neighbours cdist rule for refined points now settled? If not, delete this test, or turn it into the invariant (a refined cdist lies strictly between its neighbours).

tests.name: test_located_fixed_point_is_actually_fixed
tests.what: The solver's k=10 saddle satisfies f(p) = p to 1e-9.

tests.name: test_eigenvalues_are_saddle_like
tests.what: |stable| < 1 < |unstable| and their product is 1 (area preservation).

tests.name: test_non_convergence_raises_with_the_minpack_message
tests.what: A map with no fixed point makes compute_fixed_point raise ValueError matching 'did not converge'.
tests.concern: Only lightly coupled to the message text ('did not converge'). The test name says 'minpack message', but the match is the solver's own text.

tests.name: test_non_saddle_fixed_point_raises
tests.what: An elliptic (rotation) fixed point is rejected with a ValueError mentioning 'saddle'.

tests.name: test_orient_hook_is_honoured
tests.what: The orient hook is called once per orbit point (index 0), and its re-signed unstable eigenvector is stored while the stable one is untouched.

tests.name: test_period_three_orbit_at_k_two_is_accepted
tests.what: The exact k=2 period-3 orbit converges and every orbit point is a saddle.
tests.concern: It does not check that the orbit really has period 3 (f^3(p) = p) or the eigenvalue product, which would make it a stronger invariant test.

tests.name: test_first_point_cdist_is_euclidean_distance[x2: unstable, stable]
tests.what: The first real point of the initial segment has cdist equal to its Euclidean distance from the fixed point.
tests.concern: It pins the seeding convention (cdist starts as Euclidean distance). That is the definition of cdist's normalisation, so it is reasonable, but a change of normalisation would break it without breaking the science.

tests.name: test_iterate_law_holds_on_initial_segment[x2: unstable, stable]
tests.what: c_iterate = stretch_param * c holds on the freshly initialized segment.

tests.name: test_alpha_matches_distance_ratio[x2: unstable, stable]
tests.what: For the outer seed point, inner.cdist = outer.cdist / alpha, and alpha is the k_value-th root of the ratio across the step.
tests.concern: With k_value = 1 the second assertion is algebraically identical to the first (ratio**1 == alpha), so it is tautological on this fixture. The first assertion is a single-pair case of assert_iterate_relation.

tests.name: test_unstable_growth_preserves_invariants[x4: n_iter 1,2,4,5]
tests.what: After N unstable growth steps: strictly increasing cdist, iterate law, and acyclic consistent linked lists.
tests.concern: Fully subsumed by test_growth_integration::test_unstable_invariants_hold_at_every_step, which checks the same three invariants after each of steps 1..5. strict=True is only valid for low-stretch growth (invariants.py says ties are legitimate at folds), so it is fine on k=10 but must not spread.

tests.name: test_stable_growth_preserves_invariants[x3: n_iter 1,2,4]
tests.what: The same three invariants after N stable growth steps.
tests.concern: This is the only stable-growth step check in this shard. It could be a per-step loop like the integration test instead of three re-initialisations.

tests.name: test_cdists_are_positive_and_increasing
tests.what: The cdists of the 7-step grown unstable manifold are non-negative and sorted, with more than 3 points.
tests.concern: Weak and redundant. Sorted plus non-negative is implied by assert_cdist_monotonic(strict=True) in the parametrized tests. The docstring says 'strictly positive', but the test allows 0.

result.shard_summary: This shard covers the pure numerical core: the geometry primitives (signed area, point-in-polygon, interior point, middle node of a polyline, arc clipping, bridge orientation), batched map evaluation versus the scalar fallback, the closed-form curvature fit, the GPU backend, the refined-point cdist rule, the fixed-point solver, the initializer's cdist seeding, and the growth invariants. It has 47 test entries (60 collected cases) and the whole shard runs in about 0.6s, so cost is not a concern here. Most of it is healthy: the geometry tests use exact analytic shapes and documented policies (inclusive boundary, middle node instead of arc-length midpoint, copy not view), and the solver tests check real physics (f(p)=p, eigenvalue product = 1, saddle rejection). Overtesting is mild. There are: (a) one-line duplicates in geometry (three area-of-shape tests, a concavity test contained in the winding test, an interior-point test repeated by the crescent test); (b) private-attribute asserts (_map_batchable, _man_machine, _curvature_area, _parabolic_fit, _get_refined_point); (c) one test that pins a rule its own docstring calls suspect (the mean-of-neighbours refined cdist); (d) growth-invariant tests that repeat test_growth_integration's per-step loop, plus a redundant positive-and-sorted cdist test; (e) a tautological second assertion when k_value=1 in test_alpha_matches_distance_ratio. On the under-testing side: the oriented_bridge_polyline test never checks the orientation it claims to test, and the no-CuPy error test always skips on this machine.
gaps: oriented_bridge_polyline: nothing checks that the returned polyline actually starts at the low-cdist end (the existing test accepts either order).
enable_gpu error path never runs where CuPy is installed; it needs a monkeypatched import to be exercised.
The solver is never checked for f^k(p)=p on a period-k orbit, or for the eigenvalue product on a period-3 orbit (only saddle-ness is checked).
Nothing pins the bounds of a refined point's cdist (strictly between its neighbours), which is the real invariant behind the suspect mean rule.
The initializer's alpha/k_value relation is only exercised with k_value=1, where it is tautological; there is no initializer cdist test for k_value>1 or for an inversion saddle in this shard.
arc_polyline: no test of a window whose ends fall strictly between node cdists (interpolation vs. snapping behaviour is unspecified by tests).
The refinement-to-cutoff check covers only the unstable k=10 growth, not stable growth or a high-stretch case.

tests.name: test_grow_until_checks_the_predicate_before_growing
tests.what: grow_until with an already-true predicate returns 0 rounds and moves no point.

tests.name: test_grow_until_raises_at_the_cap
tests.what: An impossible predicate raises ValueError matching 'max iterations' after having actually grown.
tests.concern: Matches on error message text ('[Mm]ax iterations'); mild string pin, acceptable.

tests.name: test_grow_until_grows_only_the_requested_stabilities
tests.what: grow=('unstable',) leaves every stable manifold's point count unchanged and increases the unstable one.

tests.name: test_grow_until_rejects_an_empty_grow_set
tests.what: grow=() raises ValueError matching 'at least one'.
tests.concern: Argument-validation test; trivial but cheap. Could be parametrized with the other rejection tests.

tests.name: test_grow_until_requires_an_initialized_manifold
tests.what: grow_until on a fixed point with no manifolds raises 'has not been initialized'.
overlaps: tests/numerics/test_workbench_bugfixes.py::test_grow_until_intersection_honours_branch_index (same error message on a sibling driver)

tests.name: test_grow_until_preserves_crossing_ids_across_rounds
tests.what: Crossing ids held before two growth rounds still exist and point at the same coordinates (atol 1e-6) afterwards.
tests.concern: Overlaps the preserve_ids contract tested at the compute_intersections level elsewhere, but this checks it through the driver, which is the point.

tests.name: test_iterates_closed_forward_terminates
tests.what: grow_until_iterates_closed(direction='forward') ends with every target id having a +1 iterate table entry.
tests.concern: Precondition assert relies on the fixture fact that no crossing yet has a forward image; a fixture tweak turns it into a hard failure rather than a skip.

tests.name: test_iterates_closed_backward_terminates
tests.what: direction='backward' closes -1 iterates by growing only the stable manifold (unstable point count unchanged).

tests.name: test_iterates_closed_all_freezes_the_id_set
tests.what: ids='all' is frozen at call time: the original ids gain forward images while some newly born crossings remain without one.
tests.concern: The last assertion (some born crossing lacks a +1 image) depends on fixture geometry, not on the contract; if a round happened to close everything the test would fail though the freeze is correct.

tests.name: test_iterates_closed_is_a_no_op_when_already_closed
tests.what: A second call on already-closed ids returns 0 and moves no point.

tests.name: test_iterates_closed_rejects_an_unknown_id
tests.what: An id not in the registry raises ValueError 'not in the registry'.
tests.concern: Pure argument validation; fine but could join one parametrized rejection test.

tests.name: test_iterates_closed_rejects_an_unknown_direction
tests.what: direction='sideways' raises ValueError mentioning 'direction'.
tests.concern: Argument validation only.

tests.name: test_faces_closed_returns_immediately_for_interior_crossings
tests.what: grow_until_faces_closed on crossings already surrounded by closed faces returns 0 and grows nothing.

tests.name: test_faces_closed_raises_at_the_cap_for_the_anchor
tests.what: An anchor crossing never becomes interior, so grow_until_faces_closed on it hits the cap and raises.
tests.concern: Pins a KNOWN deficiency (the arrangement's anchor model leaves u-/s- slots as virtual stubs; the 'Inversion caveat' deferred Dev Note). Fixing that deferred item legitimately breaks this test. It is also the slowest test in the shard (~2 s) and only uses the anchor because no other reachable open-to-closed case exists. It enforces a limitation, not a contract.
tests.question: Do you want a test that pins 'an anchor can never close its faces' (a consequence of the deferred anchor/Inversion-caveat model), or should the cap behaviour of grow_until_faces_closed be tested with a cheap impossible target and this limitation documented only in the Dev Note?

tests.name: test_faces_closed_rejects_an_empty_id_set
tests.what: ids=[] raises ValueError 'at least one'.
tests.concern: Argument validation only.

tests.name: test_session_exposes_the_drivers
tests.what: TangleSession exposes the three drivers, growth rebuilds the cached trellis, and grow_until(True) returns 0 through the session.
tests.concern: Builds its own session inline (duplicates small-tangle setup); the cache-rebuild assertion duplicates the generation-cache suite; callable(getattr) checks are near-tautological given __getattr__ delegation.

tests.name: test_grow_until_recuts_existing_bridges
tests.what: After stable growth inside grow_until, every bridge still has a registered id and the full arrangement still builds (bridges remain consecutive).
tests.concern: Real regression guard; relies on Arrangement's own assertions as the oracle, which is fine. The explicit per-bridge asserts are weak (ids in registry) but the build is the real check.

tests.name: test_iterates_closed_all_is_scoped_to_the_grown_fixed_point
tests.what: ids='all' resolves to the non-anchor crossings of the grown fixed point only, excluding another saddle's crossings.
tests.concern: Calls the private helper workbench._frozen_ids directly instead of observing the driver; a rename/refactor of that helper breaks it while behaviour stays correct. The behaviour could be asserted via grow_until_iterates_closed not running to the cap.

tests.name: test_grow_until_clears_the_iterated_flag_it_invalidates
tests.what: After a recut no bridge is left marked iterated without a derivable image, and a WARNING containing 'recut the bridge set' is logged.
tests.concern: The stranded-bridge assertion is a good invariant; the caplog assertion pins exact log text ('recut the bridge set') and reads private workbench._bridges (workbench.bridges would do).

tests.name: test_unstable_invariants_hold_at_every_step
tests.what: Over 5 single growth steps the unstable manifold stays strictly cdist-monotonic, satisfies the iterate relation (rtol 1e-6) and is one-to-one.
tests.concern: Marked @slow but runs in milliseconds, so it is needlessly excluded from default runs. strict=True monotonicity conflicts with the memory note that cdist ties are tolerated (cdist-strict-monotonicity-fix) - check that strict is still intended.
tests.question: The memory note says cdist ties must be tolerated (strict monotonicity was the cause of the k=2.1 spikes). Should this per-step check use strict=False like the bridge check, or is strict monotonicity correct for the k=10 unstable manifold?

tests.name: test_bridges_individually_satisfy_invariants
tests.what: Every bridge cut on the trimmed small tangle is non-strictly cdist-monotonic and one-to-one.
tests.concern: Marked @slow though fast. Weak-ish: bridges are sub-arcs of a manifold already checked monotonic, so it mostly checks cutting does not reorder points.

tests.name: test_top_level_import_still_works
tests.what: tanglepack.TangleWorkbench and tanglepack.numerics.TangleWorkbench are the same class.
tests.concern: Import smoke; any other test using the public import already covers this.

tests.name: test_new_modules_import_cleanly
tests.what: BridgeIterator/IterateInference modules export their classes and graphviz exposes the two graph functions.
tests.concern: Pins the internal module layout of a completed refactor (Phase 8); a future reorganisation breaks it with no behaviour change.

tests.name: test_moved_bodies_live_in_their_new_module [x8]
tests.what: Each listed workbench method is a <45-line forwarder in TangleWorkbench.py whose name also appears in the collaborator module/class.
tests.concern: Inspects source files and counts source lines (<45) - a pure code-organisation pin of a one-time refactor. Adding a docstring or moving code back would fail it with identical behaviour. Should not be enforced by the test suite.

tests.name: test_delegating_signatures_unchanged [x7]
tests.what: Seven workbench methods have exactly the listed positional parameter names.
tests.concern: Freezes signatures as of the split; adding an optional kwarg (a legitimate API extension) fails it. Behavioural tests already call these methods.

tests.name: test_visualize_signature_unchanged
tests.what: visualize_intersection_graph has exactly the listed 11 parameter names in order.
tests.concern: Pins a plotting signature verbatim; any new keyword option fails it.

tests.name: test_collaborators_are_wired_to_their_workbench
tests.what: workbench._bridge_iterator and _iterate_inference are instances of the collaborators and back-reference the workbench.
tests.concern: Asserts private attributes and internal wiring.

tests.name: test_iterate_bridge_still_patchable_on_the_workbench
tests.what: iterate_all_bridges routes every call through workbench.iterate_bridge, so monkeypatching that attribute intercepts each bridge.
tests.concern: Exists to protect other tests' monkeypatching technique (blast-recovery tests); a test-infrastructure guard, not a behaviour. Keep only if those tests still rely on that patch point.
tests.question: Do the blast-recovery tests still monkeypatch workbench.iterate_bridge? If so, keep this guard next to them (or have them assert the spy was hit); if not, delete it.

tests.name: test_bridge_endpoints_stay_on_the_bridges_own_branch
tests.what: On the period-3 tangle every keyed bridge's endpoints are distinct registered crossings on its own unstable branch whose unstable cdists lie inside the bridge's span.
tests.concern: Good invariant ('every bridge is an arc between consecutive crossings on one unstable branch'). Reads private workbench._intersection_registry (public intersection_registry exists). Holds by construction since plan 2.2, so it partly duplicates bridge-cutting tests.

tests.name: test_trim_stable_manifolds_without_crossings
tests.what: trim_stable_manifolds on a stable-only workbench with zero crossings leaves every tail unchanged (no crash on empty max).
tests.concern: Uses private _iter_manifolds and _intersection_registry; otherwise a genuine edge-case guard.

tests.name: test_trim_stable_manifolds_cuts_just_past_the_outermost_crossing
tests.what: After trimming, the stable tail is exactly the low node of the outermost crossing segment (identity via Tangle._intersecting_segments/_manifold_segs/_seg_lookup) and is at or past the outermost crossing.
tests.concern: Computes the expected tail from the R-tree's private index structures (_intersecting_segments, _manifold_segs, _seg_lookup) - but the trim now reads the registry, so the oracle is a stale implementation path. The second assertion (tail cdist >= outermost crossing) is the contract and is already tested in test_single_source_of_truth.

tests.name: test_grow_until_intersection_stops_once_a_crossing_exists
tests.what: grow_until_intersection returns once the Tangle has at least one intersecting segment.
tests.concern: Asserts on the private Tangle._intersecting_segments rather than the registry/public crossing API.

tests.name: test_grow_until_intersection_raises_at_the_cap
tests.what: grow_until_intersection with max_iterations=1 raises ValueError 'Max iterations'.
tests.concern: Same cap contract as grow_until and grow_until_arclength; one parametrized test over the drivers would do.

tests.name: test_grow_until_intersection_honours_branch_index
tests.what: branch_index=1 on an uninitialized branch raises 'has not been initialized' instead of silently growing branch 0.

tests.name: test_grow_until_arclength_raises_at_the_cap
tests.what: grow_until_arclength with an unreachable length raises 'Max iterations'.
tests.concern: Duplicate of the cap contract across drivers.

tests.name: test_grow_until_arclength_returns_when_long_enough
tests.what: After grow_until_arclength(length=1.0) the unstable tail's cdist is >= 1.0.

tests.name: test_grown_until_intersection_is_gone
tests.what: The old misspelt method name grown_until_intersection no longer exists on the workbench.
tests.concern: Tombstone test for a completed rename; asserts absence of a name, which protects nothing scientifically.

tests.name: test_advance_key_returns_the_next_orbit_point
tests.what: On the period-3 fixture advance_key cycles orbit index 2->0 and 0->1 with branch fixed, period-1 advance is identity, and the deleted _advance_key_forward delegate is absent.
tests.concern: Fully covered by the dedicated advance_key unit tests in test_fixed_point.py (which need no session); the hasattr tombstone adds nothing. Builds the period-3 session just for a pure-function check.

tests.name: test_min_separation_drops_close_bridges
tests.what: A 3-iteration blast with min_separation=0.02 drops >0 bridges, the per-step discarded_too_close counts sum to too_close, and 3 iterations complete.
tests.concern: Weak: the comment claims 'every kept bridge respects the separation' but no assertion checks distances - the actual guard contract is untested. too_close>0 is a fixture fact for the threshold 0.02. Marked @slow but runs in ~0.15 s.

tests.name: test_min_separation_none_is_unchanged_default
tests.what: A default (min_separation=None) one-iteration blast drops nothing for proximity.

tests.name: test_iterating_fixed_point_bridge_returns_existing_copies
tests.what: Iterating the bridge anchored at fp1 returns children that are all already registered bridge objects and adds none.
tests.concern: Relies on the fixture fact that the anchor bridge's image re-traces only already-grown curve (true for this fixture; would fail if the image extended past the grown unstable tip). Marked @slow but fast.

tests.name: test_workbench_keeps_single_copy_per_bridge
tests.what: After a 3-step blast every non-partial bridge id is unique, bridge(bid) returns that object, and bridges on one unstable branch never overlap in cdist span.
tests.concern: Strong invariant check (single copy + non-overlap). Natural candidate for a shared invariant helper applied after any blast fixture.

tests.name: test_blast_recognizes_already_known_bridges
tests.what: A 2-step blast reports already_known > 0 and the per-step already_known lists sum to the total.
tests.concern: Mostly bookkeeping consistency (sum of steps == total) plus a fixture fact (>0). Does not check that the known bridges were not re-iterated, which is the claimed behaviour.

result.shard_summary: This shard (56 collected tests across 6 files, about 4.5 s for everything, so nothing in it is expensive) covers the numerics growth drivers (grow_until, grow_until_iterates_closed / faces_closed / intersection / arclength), the stable-manifold trim, bridge single-copy and non-overlap after blasts, the blast proximity guard, and the Phase 8 TangleWorkbench split. Strengths: test_grow_until.py is mostly well-designed contract testing — predicate checked before growth, cap raises only after growth, stability selection, id preservation, the frozen 'all' set, and the recut regression — and test_blast_no_overlap's single-copy/non-overlap check is a real invariant. Overtesting: all of test_workbench_split.py (8 + 7 parametrized cases plus 4 more tests) pins code organisation from a completed refactor: source file location, a forwarder shorter than 45 lines, exact parameter lists, and private collaborator wiring. All of it should go. There are also tombstone 'name is gone' tests (grown_until_intersection, _advance_key_forward). The trim test computes its expected tail from private R-tree internals even though trim now reads the registry. advance_key is re-tested here on a full period-3 session although test_fixed_point.py covers it as a unit. Smaller issues: private-attribute access (_frozen_ids, _bridges, _intersection_registry, Tangle._intersecting_segments) and one exact log-message assertion. Under-testing / weak spots: the proximity-guard test never checks distances (its comment promises a check that is not there), and the already-known test only checks counters. The anchor faces-closed test pins a known deferred deficiency (the Inversion-caveat anchor model). Five of the tests are marked @slow but each takes milliseconds, so the default run skips them for no reason. The cap and argument-validation tests are spread across files and should be one parametrized table.
gaps: No test asserts the actual min_separation guarantee: that kept sibling bridges are at least min_separation apart (the comment in test_min_separation_drops_close_bridges promises it but asserts nothing).
No test checks that bridges recognized as already_known during a blast are not re-iterated or double-counted; only the counter bookkeeping is checked.
grow_until_faces_closed has no test of a genuine open-to-closed transition (acknowledged in the module note); its only cap test relies on the anchor deficiency.
grow_until's 'recompute crossings + re-infer iterate table each round' is checked only indirectly; no test checks that iterate-table entries for preserved ids stay correct after a round.
There is no growth-driver test on an inversion (num_branches=2) saddle, for example grow_until_iterates_closed where advance_key flips branch.
trim_stable_manifolds on a multi-branch / period-3 fixture is not tested in this shard (only k=10 branch 0).

tests.name: test_reference_pairs_found_on_clean_interval
tests.what: On a hand-built period-1 window with no punctures, both consecutive window pairs are returned as reference pairs on the stable branch.

tests.name: test_direct_intersection_punctures_interval
tests.what: A crossing whose unstable cdist lies inside a pair's open unstable interval rejects that pair.

tests.name: test_iterate_punctures_interval
tests.what: A crossing whose forward iterate (scaled by lambda) lands inside the interval rejects the pair.

tests.name: test_endpoint_iterates_do_not_disqualify
tests.what: A noisy iterate of a pair member (both scaled cdists collide) does not puncture; a half-matching point does.
tests.concern: Depends on the collision_rtol tolerance value (0.1% noise passes, far stable fails); a tolerance retune could flip it, though the case is chosen with wide margin.

tests.name: test_pair_on_different_unstable_branches_rejected
tests.what: Consecutive stable-branch points on different unstable branches are not a pseudoneighbor pair.
tests.concern: Weak: asserts only that (r_n, x1) is absent, which could also happen by a puncture or window miss rather than the branch rule; the fixture's cdists are odd (r_end unstable_cdist 2.0 equal to x1, mid stable_cdist '2.0*(2.0/2.0)'), suggesting hand-edits. Does not confirm the rest of the result.

tests.name: test_branch_residue_gates_iterates
tests.what: Period-3: a candidate only lands on the target unstable branch at step counts matching its cycle residue, with a control that the same cdist on branch 0 punctures.

tests.name: test_walk_stops_at_reference_window_end
tests.what: Crossings beyond r_{n+p} (below the window) are not included in reference pairs.

tests.name: test_reference_end_fallback_by_cdist_match
tests.what: Without iterate links, r_{n+p} is located by scaled-cdist matching and the same two pairs are returned.
tests.concern: Near-duplicate of test_reference_pairs_found_on_clean_interval minus the register_iterate link; could be parametrized on link/no-link.

tests.name: test_heteroclinic_candidate_ignored
tests.what: A candidate whose unstable side belongs to another fixed point cannot puncture this tangle's intervals.

tests.name: test_unknown_unstable_branch_is_conservative
tests.what: A candidate with manifold_a_key None is tested at every residue and still punctures.
tests.concern: Pins a conservative policy for keyless (iterated-bridge) crossings; reasonable but a design choice.

tests.name: test_reference_window_starts_at_chosen_strong_pip
tests.what: With a strong pip set, the window starts at the pip and crossings beyond the cut neither appear nor puncture.
tests.concern: Sets trellis.strong_pip directly (attribute) rather than via set_strong_pip; minor.

tests.name: test_single_reference_window_per_fixed_point
tests.what: Period-3: references live only on the pip's (outermost) branch; extension yields the branch-1 image pairs at iterate 1 via cdist fallback.
tests.concern: Ties to the period-k behaviour whose hole-punching side (+1..+(k-1)) is PROVISIONAL; the extension contract itself (records forward pairs) is stated as permanent in CLAUDE.md, so the test is OK, but it is the closest test to the revisitable rule.
tests.question: If the period-k +1..+(k-1) exemption is revisited, should references still be computed only on the pip's branch (this test), or per branch?

tests.name: test_backward_iterate_punctures_interval
tests.what: A candidate's backward iterate landing inside the interval rejects the pair even when its stable position is beyond the pip cut.

tests.name: test_trajectory_extension_forward_with_dedup
tests.what: extend_pseudoneighbor_trajectories maps a reference forward through the iterate table into non-reference pairs, stopping at the chain end.
tests.concern: Name says 'with dedup' but no duplicate input is constructed, so dedup is not actually exercised.

tests.name: test_forward_unstable_branch_cycle_matches_orbit_order
tests.what: forward_unstable_branch_cycle for a period-3 no-inversion point lists orbit indices 0,1,2.
tests.concern: Thin wrapper around FixedPoint.branch_cycle; likely duplicated by numerics branch_cycle/advance_key tests.

tests.name: test_trellis_wrapper_populates_and_clears_slots
tests.what: Trellis.compute_pseudoneighbors stores references in its slot and clear_results empties pseudoneighbors.

tests.name: test_henon_reference_pairs_are_structurally_valid
tests.what: On the real k=10 tangle every reference pair is consecutive on both its stable and unstable branch and lies within [s_max/lambda, s_max].
tests.concern: Good invariant test; could move to an invariant suite alongside test_topology_invariants henon_punched checks.

tests.name: test_strong_pip_cuts_warn_when_branches_are_left_uncut
tests.what: Private _strong_pip_cuts on a period-3 pip with no iterate table cuts only branch 0 at cdist 1.0 and logs a WARNING containing the pip id and 'k_value 3'.
tests.concern: Calls a private helper and asserts on log message substrings; the warning text and the 'every branch should be cut' expectation may conflict with the 2026-09-30 rule that only the pip's own branch is unified for period-k orbits.
tests.question: For a period-k orbit, is a pip leaving k-1 stable branches uncut still a condition worth WARNING about (and testing via log text), or is it now expected behaviour given the pip-branch-only fundamental segment?

tests.name: test_strong_pip_cuts_are_silent_when_every_branch_is_cut
tests.what: Private _strong_pip_cuts on a period-1 pip emits no 'k_value' warning.
tests.concern: Private function plus negative log-text assertion (filters on substring 'k_value'); passes trivially if the message wording changes. Merge with the warning test as one parametrized case or drop with it.

tests.name: test_table_linked_deep_iterate_does_not_disqualify
tests.what: A pair member's own 6-step iterate with 2% stable drift is recognised by iterate-table lookup and does not puncture; unlinked, the collision fallback rejects the pair.
tests.concern: Encodes the user rule 'lookup first, never the map' (2026-09-15) and the k=2.8 8-blast regression; the unlinked half pins that collision_rtol < 2%, a tolerance detail.

tests.name: test_table_linked_landing_uses_registered_cdist
tests.what: When the table links a candidate's landing, the registered cdist (4.5, outside) decides over the scaled estimate (3.0, inside); unlinked it punctures.

tests.name: test_heteroclinic_crossing_does_not_disqualify_strong_pip
tests.what: A heteroclinic crossing (other fixed point's unstable side) inside q0's box does not block q0 from being a strong pip.

tests.name: test_homoclinic_crossing_still_disqualifies_strong_pip
tests.what: Control: the same geometry with a homoclinic blocker disqualifies q0 and reports the blocker id.
tests.concern: Could be parametrized with the heteroclinic test (unstable owner fp1 vs fp3 vs None).

tests.name: test_missing_unstable_key_disqualifier_is_kept
tests.what: A blocker with no unstable key is treated as part of the tangle and disqualifies q0.
tests.concern: Same structure as the two above; parametrize.

tests.name: test_table_linked_own_iterate_does_not_disqualify_strong_pip
tests.what: q0's own drifted forward image is recognised by iterate-table lookup and does not block; unlinked it blocks via collision fallback.
tests.concern: Unlinked half pins collision_rtol < 2% (a tolerance detail).

tests.name: test_classify_strong_pips_all_fixed_points

tests.concern: Builds the heavy-named nested p3 fixture (cheap here, ~0.1s) just to check the dict shape.

tests.name: test_trellis_auto_rebuilds_after_registry_change

tests.concern: Exact duplicate of the cache-miss case in test_session_trellis_cache.py; misfiled under strong pips.

tests.name: test_plot_helpers_cover_every_tangle

tests.concern: Smoke test of plotting fan-out; handle count is the only assertion.

tests.name: test_plot_helpers_draw_pairs_and_holes

tests.concern: Asserts a private attribute (_built_generation); the identity check alone is the contract.

tests.name: test_reads_do_not_invalidate_the_cache

tests.name: test_rebuild_flag_forces_a_miss

tests.concern: One of six near-identical mutation->miss tests; parametrize over a mutation table like numerics/test_generation_and_caches.MUTATIONS. Slowest test in shard (0.6s).

tests.name: test_compute_intersections_invalidates_the_cache
tests.what: compute_intersections yields a new trellis bound to the new registry.
tests.concern: Duplicate of test_session_strong_pips::test_trellis_auto_rebuilds_after_registry_change.

tests.name: test_iterate_bridge_invalidates_the_cache
tests.what: Iterating a bridge yields a new cached trellis.
tests.concern: Part of the mutation family; parametrize.

tests.name: test_rebuild_bridges_invalidates_the_cache
tests.what: rebuild_bridges yields a new cached trellis.
tests.concern: Part of the mutation family; parametrize.
