tests.what: Adding a resonance zone (at an arbitrary registry id) yields a new cached trellis.
tests.concern: Uses registry.all_ids()[0] as the zone pip, an arbitrary and possibly non-pip crossing; the test passes only because zone creation mutates, not because the input is meaningful.

tests.name: test_restore_invalidates_the_cache
tests.what: ResonanceZone.restore yields a new cached trellis (the gap manual invalidation used to leave).

tests.name: test_invalidate_trellises_is_a_deprecated_no_op
tests.what: invalidate_trellises emits DeprecationWarning matching 'no-op' and does not drop the cache.
tests.concern: Tests a deprecated alias 'kept for one release'; matches warning text. Dies with the alias.
tests.question: invalidate_trellises was deprecated 'for one release' — can the alias and this test be removed now?

result.shard_summary: This shard (46 tests, all fast: the whole shard runs in about 2.5s) covers the Compute-Pseudoneighbors algorithm (21 synthetic and one Hénon test), strong-pip classification restricted to a single tangle (4 synthetic), the session fan-out facades for strong pips, pseudoneighbors, holes and partitions (11), and the generation-keyed Trellis cache (10). Its main strength is the synthetic hand-built registries in test_pseudoneighbor.py and test_strong_pip_periodic_point.py. Each one pins one algorithmic rule with a control case: direct, forward, backward and residue-gated punctures, the heteroclinic and keyless candidate policies, and the 'lookup first' iterate-table rule. They are cheap, exact by construction and tied to scientific contracts rather than fixture facts. There is little overtesting here. The weak spots: (1) two tests call the private _strong_pip_cuts and assert on WARNING text. That warning (period-k pip leaves k-1 branches uncut) may no longer describe an error under the 2026-09-30 pip-branch-only rule. (2) The cache-miss tests are six copies of one pattern and could be one parametrized table. One of them duplicates test_session_strong_pips::test_trellis_auto_rebuilds_after_registry_change, and together they mirror numerics/test_generation_and_caches MUTATIONS one layer up. (3) The facade tests split the dict-vs-list return convention into separate tests, and two of them are vacuous on empty results. (4) A few tests read private state (_built_generation), test a deprecated alias, or depend on the collision_rtol size (the unlinked halves of the table-linked tests). (5) test_pair_on_different_unstable_branches_rejected has a muddled fixture and a single negative assertion that could pass for the wrong reason. There are no colour or coordinate pins and no expensive fixture reruns.
gaps: No direct test of strong-pip candidate SELECTION (which candidate set_strong_pip/the default picks, e.g. outermost) at the unit level; only implicit via session tests and _define_zone.
No positive-case unit test of the strong-pip box criterion on its own (a clean box that is a strong pip, or a blocker on a different stable branch); only the heteroclinic/homoclinic/keyless variants.
is_strong_pip under an inversion fixed point (k_value == 2*period, branch flip in advance_key) is not tested; all synthetic fixed points are no-inversion.
Pseudoneighbor computation under inversion / orientation-reversing maps is not tested.
extend_pseudoneighbor_trajectories dedup is claimed in a test name but never exercised with duplicate inputs; backward extension (if any) untested.
No test that two different pips on one branch raise, or that the same pip gathered twice counts once (CLAUDE.md fundamental-segment rule) in this shard.
Cache: no test that trellis() vs trellis([fp]) selections cache independently, and none that set_strong_pip changes the dual_graph cache key (covered maybe elsewhere).
No test that the registry-replacing compute_intersections(preserve_ids=True) keeps pseudoneighbor results consistent across a rebuild.

tests.name: test_registry_generation_bumps_on_add
tests.what: IntersectionRegistry.generation increases after add().

tests.name: test_registry_generation_bumps_on_add_synthetic
tests.what: generation increases after add_synthetic().
tests.concern: Same shape as the other three registry-bump tests; four functions for one contract.

tests.name: test_registry_generation_bumps_on_register_iterate
tests.what: generation increases after register_iterate().

tests.name: test_registry_generation_bumps_on_reindex_from
tests.what: generation increases after reindex_from() (the preserve_ids path).

tests.name: test_registry_generation_stands_still_on_a_deduped_add
tests.what: A duplicate add (collision) stores nothing and leaves generation unchanged.
tests.concern: Is a stricter rule than the cache contract needs: an extra bump would only cost a spurious cache rebuild, not correctness. It does indirectly pin dedup behaviour, though.

tests.name: test_registry_generation_stands_still_on_reads
tests.what: Calling nine read accessors on the registry does not bump generation.
tests.concern: Enumerates the current read API by name (on_cdist_range, nearest_by_unstable_cdist, graph...), so renaming or removing any of them breaks the test even though the contract still holds.

tests.name: test_registry_orderings_and_ranks_track_insertions
tests.what: by_unstable/by_stable orderings, ranks and nearest_by_unstable_cdist are correct after out-of-order inserts.
tests.concern: Belongs with the registry tests rather than the generation/cache file.

tests.name: test_registry_insert_is_near_linear
tests.what: Registry passes a wall-clock check: 20k synthetic inserts take under 2 s, and the last 1k block is less than 15x slower than the first.
tests.concern: A wall-clock performance assertion in the correctness suite. It already flaked once (fixed with gc.collect) and depends on machine load. It also adds 20k inserts to every run.
tests.question: Should performance guards like this move to an opt-in benchmark marker (e.g. @pytest.mark.perf, excluded by default) instead of the default suite?

tests.name: test_workbench_generation_bumps_on_every_mutation[8 params]
tests.what: Each of 8 workbench mutation methods (register_manifold, grow_n_times, compute_intersections, create/clear/rebuild_bridges, iterate_bridge, trim_stable_manifolds) bumps workbench.generation.
tests.concern: The grow_n_times param takes 0.9 s. Each param rebuilds the henon_tangle_with_bridges fixture, which is function-scoped. This is the real contract behind the session caches, though.

tests.name: test_workbench_generation_stands_still_on_reads
tests.what: Nine read paths (bridges, bridge(id), image_bridges, point arrays...) leave workbench.generation unchanged.
tests.concern: Pins the read-API names; it also reads the misspelled 'uniiterated_bridges' attribute, so fixing the typo would break the test.

tests.name: test_workbench_generation_bumps_when_a_manifold_tail_moves
tests.what: Re-assigning a manifold's tail (setter bumps version) bumps workbench.generation.
tests.concern: Self-assignment 'tail = tail' counts as a mutation, which ties the test to the setter-bumps-unconditionally implementation. Still a reasonable way to test that geometry feeds the generation.

tests.name: test_bridge_point_array_is_memoised
tests.what: Two get_point_array() calls return the identical object (memo hit) and it equals a fresh _walk_nodes walk.
tests.concern: The `is` identity check pins the memoisation strategy, and the test calls the private _walk_nodes. The equality half is the real contract and is covered more strongly by test_point_arrays_reflect_growth.

tests.name: test_point_arrays_reflect_growth
tests.what: After growth, manifold and every bridge point array equal an un-memoised walk, and at least one bridge gained points (memo invalidation works).
tests.concern: The 'grew' assertion depends on refinement landing inside an existing bridge on this fixture (a fixture fact), but it is what makes the check non-vacuous.

tests.name: test_node_walk_is_not_shared_between_callers
tests.what: Mutating the list returned by get_point_array(return_nodes=True) does not corrupt the memo.

tests.name: test_branch_position_map_is_memoised
tests.what: FixedPoint.branch_position_map returns the same object twice, with k equal to k_value.
tests.concern: The `is` identity assertion pins a caching choice, not behaviour; the useful content is the k_value equality.

tests.name: test_branch_memo_is_invalidated_by_set_k_value
tests.what: After negating the eigenvalues and calling set_k_value, branch_position_map and branch_cycle report k=2 rather than the stale k=1.
tests.concern: Builds an artificial inversion by flipping the eigenvalue signs. That is fine for testing invalidation, but the asserted k_before==1 / k_after==2 is a fact about the k=10 fixture.

tests.name: test_bridge_point_arrays_survive_an_iterate
tests.what: iterate_bridge bumps the version of every registered bridge, and each memoised array still equals a fresh walk.
tests.concern: Requiring every bridge's version to bump pins a blanket-invalidation strategy. The docstring admits the scenario never occurs on this fixture, so a smarter, targeted invalidation would fail the test while staying correct. The array-equals-walk half is the real contract.
tests.question: Is 'every bridge's memo is dropped on any iterate' a rule you want, or only 'memos never go stale'? The latter permits targeted invalidation later.

tests.name: test_bridge_cutting_pin_k10
tests.what: The k=10 fixture produces exactly 8 registry entries, and the 7 bridges' endpoint cdists match 6-significant-digit values captured before the Phase 2 refactor.
tests.concern: Exact float pins (6 sig. digits) on growth and refinement output, kept as a migration check for a refactor that finished in Sept 2026. Any change to refinement tolerance, seed step or growth will break it even when the science is right. Invariants elsewhere (bridge ids ordered, consecutive crossings, unstable x stable) already cover correctness.
tests.question: The Phase 2 refactor is done. Should the pre-refactor cdist fingerprints (k=10 and p3) be deleted, or kept as a deliberate golden-master that you re-record whenever numerics change?

tests.name: test_bridge_cutting_pin_period_3
tests.what: Nested period-3 session: 34 registry entries and 30 bridges' endpoint cdists match 6-digit pre-refactor values.
tests.concern: Same golden-master issue as the k=10 pin, with 30 rows of floats on a deeper p3 tangle that is more sensitive to solver and refinement tweaks. Marked slow.
tests.question: Same as the k=10 pin: delete, or keep as a re-recordable golden master?

tests.name: test_tangle_keeps_only_index_state
tests.what: Checks private attributes on Tangle: five named ones must be absent and seven named ones must be present.
tests.concern: Entirely private attribute names: '_rtree', '_seg_lookup' and the other five kept names must exist, and the 5 removed names must not. Renaming any private field breaks it. The 'gone' half is a refactor tombstone. The real contract (crossings live only in the registry) is better shown behaviourally.

tests.name: test_compute_intersections_returns_one_coord_per_registered_crossing
tests.what: compute_intersections returns one coord per registry entry, in all_ids order, and each equals the registry's coords.
tests.concern: Pins that the return value is ordered by all_ids. Minor, but fine.

tests.name: test_every_registered_crossing_carries_its_unstable_segment
tests.what: Every registered crossing has an unstable_manifold and an unstable_segment whose cdists bracket its unstable_cdist.

tests.name: test_trim_stable_manifolds_reads_the_registry
tests.what: After trimming, the stable tail's cdist is at or past the outermost registered stable cdist.
tests.concern: Only checks the lower bound: a no-op trim would also pass, so it does not show anything was trimmed.

tests.name: test_bridge_endpoints_are_the_ids_of_the_crossings_it_was_cut_at
tests.what: Every bridge is non-partial with int endpoints in unstable-cdist order, contained in its own root..tail cdist span; two removed private helpers must not exist.
tests.concern: The two hasattr(not) checks on removed private helpers are refactor tombstones. The ordering and int-id checks duplicate test_bridge_identity's id-ordering test. The containment check is the new part.

tests.name: test_partial_bridge_reports_its_missing_endpoint
tests.what: Iterating bridges eventually yields a partial child, which lacks one endpoint but keeps its manifold_key.
tests.concern: Relies on the k=10 fixture producing a partial at the frontier (a fixture fact). Largely overlaps test_bridge_identity's partial-pieces test.

tests.name: test_base_manifold_requires_a_manifold_key
tests.what: Constructing BaseManifold or Bridge without manifold_key raises TypeError.
tests.concern: Pins the exception type (TypeError from a missing required kwarg); minor.

tests.name: test_register_manifold_rejects_a_mismatched_key
tests.what: register_manifold raises an AssertionError when the key differs from the manifold's own key.
tests.concern: Relies on an `assert` statement, so it fails under `python -O`. The author does treat asserts as the main correctness guard, though.

tests.name: test_iterated_bridge_crossings_carry_the_advanced_key
tests.what: On the p3 tangle, the first bridge whose iterate creates new crossings has every new crossing and child carrying advance_key(parent key, 1).
tests.concern: Only checks the first productive bridge. A good key-propagation contract.

tests.name: test_bridge_endpoint_iterates_are_registered_explicitly
tests.what: iterate_bridge registers n=1 iterate-table links for both parent endpoints. Each image is the new crossing nearest map(source), within 1e-3 of the scale, with the runner-up more than 0.1 of the scale away. Each image lies on advance_key of the stable branch, and the two images differ.
tests.concern: Calls the map in a test (fine in numerics). The 1e-3 and 0.1 scale margins are calibrated to this fixture; the runner-up margin in particular could fail on a denser blast while the code stays correct.

tests.name: test_every_getter_matches_an_independent_walk[2 params: unstable, stable]
tests.what: Each of the five BaseManifold array getters (point, cdist, non-iterated point/cdist, iterated point) equals a hand-rolled linked-list walk with the matching filter.
tests.concern: Good behavioural test. It pins the quirk that get_cdist_array ignores the tail (documented on the getter).

tests.name: test_final_node_truncates_the_point_walk
tests.what: get_point_array(final_node=x) returns the walk prefix up to and including x.

tests.name: test_collect_is_the_only_traversal
tests.what: Monkeypatching the private _collect to raise makes all five getters raise.
tests.concern: Pins private structure: it requires that every getter route through a method named _collect. Behaviour is already covered by test_every_getter_matches_an_independent_walk; renaming or restructuring the walker breaks this test with no behaviour change.

tests.name: test_string_dispatched_iter_method_is_gone
tests.what: BaseManifold has no _iter_method, and no numerics source file contains the text '_iter_method('.
tests.concern: Refactor tombstone. It greps source text for a removed private name and adds no protection beyond review.

tests.name: test_collect_rejects_a_broken_iterate_link
tests.what: Swaps a node's class at runtime so it claims an iterate that is None; get_iterated_point_array must then raise ValueError matching 'NoneType'.
tests.concern: Fragile runtime __class__ surgery, and the restore depends on the MRO index. It matches an exception message ('NoneType') that comes from numpy or the implementation, not a designed error, so it tests an accidental failure mode.
tests.question: Should a broken iterate link raise a designed error (custom message or assertion) that tests can rely on, or is this check not worth keeping?

tests.name: test_first_node_steps_past_the_root_branch_point
tests.what: For a BranchPoint root, first_node() and first_node(1) return the corresponding forward_branches entries.

tests.name: test_first_node_on_an_ordinary_root_is_the_root
tests.what: first_node() on an ordinary (non-BranchPoint) root returns the root itself.

tests.name: test_first_node_needs_a_branch_index
tests.what: first_node() on a BranchPoint root with branch_index=None raises ValueError mentioning branch_index.

tests.name: test_stability_alias_is_defined_once_in_numerics
tests.what: A regex over source text finds 'Stability = Literal' only in numerics/Intersection.py, and two re-exports are identical to it.
tests.concern: A code-style lint written as a test (regex on source files). It would fail if the alias moved (e.g. to a types.py) even though nothing behaves differently. It belongs in a linter, if anywhere.

tests.name: test_henon_factories_match_the_closed_form
tests.what: henon_map/inverse/jacobian match the closed form at one point; inverse(map(p)) = p; det J = b.

tests.name: test_henon_factories_are_batch_capable_on_axis_zero
tests.what: henon_map accepts a (2, N) batch and agrees column-by-column with the single-point calls.

tests.name: test_saddle_guesses_converge_to_real_fixed_points[3 params]
tests.what: Each recorded saddle guess (k10 saddle, k10 inversion, p3 saddle) converges under construct_fixed_point to a true fixed point of the map.
tests.concern: Asserts f(x) = x even for the 'p3 saddle' case. If that point is genuinely period 3 the check only passes because the param name is misleading; worth checking that the p3 guess really is a period-1 point (HENON_P3's outer saddle).

tests.name: test_saddle_guesses_returns_a_fresh_copy
tests.what: Mutating the returned guess dict does not affect the next call; the k10 saddle guess equals [4, -4].
tests.concern: Pins the literal [4, -4] guess value; comparing against a first, unmutated call would test the copy semantics without it.

tests.name: test_saddle_guesses_refuses_unknown_parameters
tests.what: saddle_guesses(3.7, 1) raises KeyError matching 'no recorded saddle guesses'.
tests.concern: Pins the message text; it also breaks if someone records guesses for k=3.7.

tests.name: test_no_test_or_script_defines_its_own_henon
tests.what: A regex scan of tests/ and scripts/ finds no 'def henon*(point)' style local Henon definitions.
tests.concern: A repo-hygiene lint written as a test. It scans scripts (not library code), and CLAUDE.md says the notebooks still carry their own copies, so the rule is already partial. It fails on a harmless helper name match.
tests.question: Do you want repo-hygiene rules (one Henon definition, one Stability alias, no _iter_method) enforced by pytest, or should they become lint/CI checks, or be dropped?

tests.name: test_fundamental_segments_have_injective_cdist
tests.what: Both fundamental segments from the initializer have at least 3 nodes and no cdist collision.
tests.concern: Memory notes record that cdist ties are legitimate (the strict-monotonicity fix was reverted; the correct invariant is geometric no-spike, not injectivity). On the fundamental segment injectivity is safe.

tests.name: test_low_stretch_growth_keeps_cdist_injective
tests.what: After 2 growth iterations at k=10, neither manifold has a cdist collision (1e-12 tolerance).
tests.concern: Enforces cdist injectivity, which the memory note calls not the correct invariant. It is scoped to low stretch, but a refinement change that legitimately produces ties would fail it.
tests.question: Given the 2026 finding that cdist ties are tolerated (the invariant is geometric no-spike), should any test enforce cdist injectivity after growth, even at low stretch?

tests.name: test_area_preserved_along_every_recorded_iterate_chain
tests.what: For every crossing with an n=1 iterate link, the product unstable_cdist*stable_cdist is preserved along the chain (rtol 1e-3).
tests.concern: Since infer_iterates matches by predicted cdists, this is partly circular: it confirms the matcher's own tolerance. Still a valid area-preservation guard.

tests.name: test_area_preserved_helper_rejects_a_broken_chain
tests.what: Corrupting one image's unstable cdist makes assert_area_preserved_along_chain raise.
tests.concern: Tests the test helper itself (meta-test). Cheap and makes the positive test meaningful.

result.shard_summary:
This shard has 46 test functions (58 collected items, about 4 s total, nothing slow except the two p3-session tests and the 0.9 s grow param). It covers four refactor-era numerics files: the generation counter and memo caches (Phase 4), single sources of truth for crossings, bridge endpoints and manifold keys (Phase 2), the walker / Stability alias / shared Henon cleanup (Phase 8A), and two meta-tests for the invariants.py helpers.

**Strengths:**
- The generation-bump contract is behavioural and well parametrized over mutations.
- Point-array memos are compared against an independent walk after growth and iterate.
- Manifold-key propagation, explicit endpoint-iterate registration and the area-product chain check are real contracts.

**Overtesting comes in three clusters:**
1. Refactor tombstones and private-structure pins: hasattr on removed or kept private Tangle attributes, the monkeypatched _collect, a source grep for _iter_method, the regex lint on the Stability alias, the regex lint on per-file Henon definitions, and hasattr(not) on removed workbench helpers. These fail on harmless renames and protect nothing behaviourally.
2. Golden-master float pins: the K10 and P3 bridge-endpoint fingerprints at 6 significant digits were captured as a pre-refactor migration check for a refactor that is finished. Any legitimate numerics change breaks them.
3. Memoisation-strategy pins: `is` identity checks, every bridge's version bumping on iterate, and a wall-clock performance assertion that has flaked before.

**Under-testing:** the trim test is weak (a no-op trim passes). The broken-iterate-link test relies on __class__ surgery and matches an accidental 'NoneType' error. One test enforces post-growth cdist injectivity even though the memory notes say ties are legitimate.

**Duplicates:** these overlap with tests/numerics/test_bridge_identity.py (id ordering, partial pieces).
gaps: No test that a cached derived view is actually rebuilt when generation moves at the numerics level: generation bumps are tested, but there is no consumer cache-miss test (that lives in tests/test_session_trellis_cache.py).
Stability of registry ids under compute_intersections(preserve_ids=True) is not exercised here; only the reindex_from generation bump is.
No test that trim_stable_manifolds actually shortens the manifold (that the tail moves inward to the outermost crossing, not just stays beyond it).
No test that compute_intersections is idempotent (calling it twice without mutation yields the same registry and does not bump generation).
The walker tests do not cover the stable-manifold iterate direction under orientation-reversing (inversion) maps; the getters are only checked on the k=10 orientation-preserving fixture.
The area-product chain check is only run on k=10, not on the p3 or inversion fixtures, where per_step_beta and branch flips matter.

tests.name: test_start_equals_goal_is_trivial
tests.what: shortest_walks with start==goal returns status 'trivial', a zero-step walk whose itinerary is (start, goal) on the start face.
tests.concern: Also pins start_faces list and walk.faces internals of the Walk dataclass; acceptable.

tests.name: test_start_face_equal_to_goal_face_is_trivial
tests.what: Two different elements on the same face give a trivial zero-crossing walk with itinerary (start, goal).
tests.concern: Near-duplicate of the start==goal trivial case; could be one parametrized 'trivial' test.

tests.name: test_single_crossing_records_entry_then_exit
tests.what: A one-node walk records entry-side then exit-side element at the crossing, even itinerary length, step fields, disjoint pairs and multiplicity 1.

tests.name: test_crossing_from_the_right_side_records_right_then_left
tests.what: Mirror of the single-crossing case: entering from the right side records R then L.
tests.concern: Mirror of the previous test; fine but a parametrize over side would merge the two.

tests.name: test_walls_are_never_crossed
tests.what: Faces joined only by open (wall) nodes are unreachable; status 'unreachable', no walks, and a WARNING containing 'unreachable'.
tests.concern: Asserts on a log message substring ('unreachable'); the status field already carries the contract, the caplog check is redundant and couples to wording.

tests.name: test_unreachable_isolated_goal
tests.what: Two disconnected unified components give status 'unreachable'.
tests.concern: Overlaps the walls test (both assert 'unreachable'); cheap and distinct cause (disconnection vs wall).

tests.name: test_merged_face_self_adjacency_is_skipped
tests.what: A unified node with the same merged face on both sides is never used as a step; the walk still has length 1.

tests.name: test_only_the_shortest_layer_is_kept
tests.what: With a direct 1-step route and a 2-step detour, only the shortest is returned (unique, length 1).

tests.name: test_tie_with_different_itineraries_is_ambiguous
tests.what: Two equally short walks with different itineraries give status 'ambiguous', both kept in deterministic order, WARNING logged, first walk is the lower element.
tests.concern: Log-substring check ('ambiguous') duplicates the status assertion; the exact ordering pin (L1 before L2) encodes the 'deterministic first' rule, which is spec (CLAUDE.md: first in deterministic order feeds the rest) but the sort key itself is an implementation choice.

tests.name: test_parallel_nodes_with_equal_elements_dedupe_to_unique
tests.what: Two parallel unified nodes carrying identical elements collapse to one walk (unique) with multiplicity 2 and no warning.

tests.name: test_no_start_node_and_no_goal_node
tests.what: Missing start / goal elements yield 'no_start_node' / 'no_goal_node', no walks, and WARNINGs mentioning 'start element' / 'goal element'.
tests.concern: Log-message substring checks are redundant with the status values.

tests.name: test_multiple_start_faces_are_all_searched
tests.what: A start element owning edges on two faces searches from both and finds the route from the second; asserts an INFO message containing the exact fragment 'faces 2 faces'.
tests.concern: The INFO-message check pins a formatting accident of the log string ('the start element faces %d faces'); rewording the log breaks the test with the algorithm unchanged. The behavioural part (start_faces, chosen walk) is the real contract.

tests.name: test_max_walks_cap_sets_truncated
tests.what: 3x3 parallel routes give 9 ambiguous walks; max_walks=4 caps to 4 with truncated=True and a WARNING containing 'truncated'.
tests.concern: Minor log-substring check, otherwise a real contract.

tests.name: test_walks_are_sorted_deterministically
tests.what: Walks come out sorted by element id regardless of node insertion order, and passing fixed_points explicitly gives the same result.
tests.concern: Determinism is a real requirement; the exact ascending-element-id order is an implementation choice (any stable order would satisfy the spec). Partly overlaps the tie test's ordering check.

tests.name: test_walk_search_repr_and_walk_repr
tests.what: repr(WalkSearch) contains 'unique' and repr(Walk) contains '1 step(s)'.
tests.concern: Pins repr strings, a pure debugging convenience; any wording change fails it while the science is unaffected.

tests.name: test_contained_landing_from_the_table
tests.what: A bounded homotopy element maps via registered table iterates to span (0.25,0.5), contained in iterated L#1, same side, from_table (True,True); also checks repr substring.
tests.concern: Exact float span is fine here (synthetic table values, exact by construction); the repr substring 'L#1 -> ' is a cosmetic pin.

tests.name: test_unbounded_low_end_maps_to_zero
tests.what: The anchor element's low end maps to cdist 0 and lands in iterated element 0.
tests.concern: Small; could merge with the other two table-landing cases into one parametrized test.

tests.name: test_outermost_element_lands_by_the_table
tests.what: The outermost bounded element lands by table lookup in span (0.5,1.0), iterated L#2.
tests.concern: Same shape as the two neighbouring landing tests.

tests.name: test_unbounded_high_end_is_scaled
tests.what: An unbounded high end is scaled by per_step_beta (4.0*0.25) when no table entry exists; from_table (True, False).

tests.name: test_scaled_end_tolerance_is_relative
tests.what: A scaled end overshooting the iterated element by 1e-3 relative is still 'contained' (SCALING_RTOL).
tests.concern: Implicitly pins SCALING_RTOL to be >= 1e-3; a legitimate tolerance tightening would break it. Note also the test's homotopy spec gives hi_id=4 yet asserts from_table (True,False) — relies on 4 having no table entry.
tests.question: Is the scaled-end tolerance (SCALING_RTOL) a deliberate contract, or a tunable that should not be pinned by a test?

tests.name: test_orientation_reversing_map_flips_the_side
tests.what: With orientation_preserving=False the landing flips to the other side; with it True the side is kept.

tests.name: test_zero_width_span_probes_its_low_end
tests.what: A degenerate non-singleton element whose ends coincide in cdist still lands (probing the low end) and is contained.
tests.concern: Exercises a hand-made degenerate case that the docstring of the code may treat as defensive; fine as an edge-case guard.

tests.name: test_singleton_lands_on_the_registered_iterate
tests.what: A singleton homotopy element maps to the singleton iterated element at its registered +1 iterate; repr mentions 'singleton'.
tests.concern: Repr substring check is cosmetic.

tests.name: test_singleton_with_unregistered_image_is_unresolved
tests.what: A singleton with no registered +1 iterate is unresolved, target None, reason contains 'not registered', WARNING logged, repr says 'unresolved'.
tests.concern: Three string checks (reason, log, repr) on the same wording 'not registered'; the resolved/target fields carry the contract.

tests.name: test_singleton_owned_by_a_non_singleton_is_info_not_warning
tests.what: Under backward-only holes, a singleton whose image is owned by a non-singleton iterated element is resolved normally, logged at INFO (message must contain 'NON-singleton' and 'backward only'), not WARNING.
tests.concern: Encodes the backward-only-holes rule, whose period-k +1..+(k-1) exemption is PROVISIONAL per CLAUDE.md; the behaviour (resolved, target L#1) is fine, but the exact INFO wording ('NON-singleton', 'backward only') is a log-message pin.
tests.question: Should the log level (INFO vs WARNING) for this case be an enforced contract, or only the resolved landing?

tests.name: test_span_straddling_two_elements_fills_covering
tests.what: A span straddling an iterated cut is resolved but not contained, target = midpoint owner, covering lists both elements, WARNING and repr contain 'straddles'.
tests.concern: CLAUDE.md says the straddle case is 'handled defensively, not modelled'; pinning covering order and the midpoint-owner target is OK, the log/repr wording is not needed.

tests.name: test_image_on_an_unexpected_branch_is_unresolved
tests.what: If a registered image crossing lies on a foreign branch the landing is unresolved with reason/log containing 'instead of'.
tests.concern: Only behavioural assertion is not resolved; the rest is message wording ('instead of').

tests.name: test_probe_outside_the_iterated_partition_is_unresolved
tests.what: A span outside the iterated partition's extent is unresolved with reason 'no single iterated element' and span (0.5,1.0).
tests.concern: Reason-string substring pin.

tests.name: test_land_element_refuses_an_unknown_ref
tests.what: land_element raises IndexError for an element id that does not exist.
tests.concern: Pins the exception type IndexError, which is just whatever list indexing raises; a refactor to KeyError/ValueError (more appropriate) would fail it.

tests.name: test_trellis_itinerary_is_even_and_alternates_rows
tests.what: trellis_itinerary over a 3-bridge chain with alternating signs yields the exact 6-element itinerary given by the row rule, entry/exit at interior crossings on opposite sides, and same-side disjoint pairs.
tests.concern: Exact itinerary is derived from the documented row rule (row(first)=left iff s>0, row(second)=left iff s<0) — a real spec pin, not a fixture fact.

tests.name: test_trellis_itinerary_direction_minus_one_reverses
tests.what: Direction -1 yields the element-wise reverse of the forward itinerary (rows read on forward BridgeId order).

tests.name: test_trellis_itinerary_single_pair
tests.what: A single-bridge chain yields a 2-element same-side itinerary.
tests.concern: Subsumed by the 3-bridge test's first pair; marginal value.

tests.name: test_trellis_itinerary_errors
tests.what: trellis_itinerary raises ValueError for empty chain, non-consecutive chain, an unowned crossing ('grow or blast') and a zero crossing sign.
tests.concern: match= regexes pin message wording; exception type alone (plus perhaps one key word) would suffice.

tests.name: test_k10_landings_and_the_active_class_walk
tests.what: On the real k=10 fixture every homotopy element lands resolved/contained on the same side, anchor elements land in element 0, the single active class has a unique 6-element unified walk of same-side pairs, and every registered member image's trellis itinerary matches the walk up to homotopy parents.
tests.concern: Strong integration test; the 'exactly 1 active class' and 'itinerary length 6' are k=10 fixture facts that change if the fixture's growth depth or the cut rule changes. Largely overlaps test_symbolic_dynamics::test_k10_every_landing_contained / test_k10_active_class_word (which also pins the exact names R_1^1 R_3^3 | L_3 L_1^2 | R_3^1 R_1^3) and the verified-evidence check there.
tests.question: Do you want one k=10 end-to-end symbolic test (in test_symbolic_dynamics) or also this lower-level DualWalk-only one?

tests.name: test_element_name_text_and_mathtext
tests.what: ElementName renders exact text/str/short_text/mathtext/tag/branch_code strings for split, plain and lettered names (e.g. 'R_(1.0;1)^2', '$R_{1.0;1}^{2}$', 'B:R_(1.0;2)^1', '${}^{B}R_{1.0;2}^{1}$').
tests.concern: Exact-string pins of a naming notation that has already changed once (2026-09-30 branch codes added). They ARE the documented format, so pinning is legitimate, but every future notation tweak will fail many asserts here; keep one canonical example per form rather than every field.
tests.question: Is the R_(o.b;i)^j / mathtext notation now stable, or should tests pin only its structural parts (side, subscript, superscript, branch, letter)?

tests.name: test_element_name_is_hashable_and_compares_by_value
tests.what: ElementName equality/hash by value, plus exact repr "ElementName('R_(0.0;1)^2')".
tests.concern: The exact repr pin is cosmetic; value equality/hash is the real contract.

tests.name: test_homotopy_names_count_anchor_outward_per_side
tests.what: Homotopy names are L_1..L_3, R_1..R_3 anchor outward with subscript = element_id+1, superscript 1, no letters for one fixed point.

tests.name: test_superscripts_follow_parent_groups_anchor_outward
tests.what: Iterated children get superscripts counting the parent's children anchor outward (L_1^1, L_1^2, R_3^1..R_3^3), unsplit print plain, len 9.

tests.name: test_unsplit_elements_print_plain
tests.what: An iterated element with no siblings prints without superscript (R_1, '$R_{0.0;1}$').
tests.concern: Already covered by the superscript test's name list and the text/mathtext test; mathtext exact string again.

tests.name: test_ref_of_name_round_trips_and_lookup_by_text
tests.what: ref_of and lookup invert name for every ref, short-form lookup works when unambiguous, unknown names raise KeyError.

tests.name: test_parent_of_and_children_of_round_trip
tests.what: children_of is sorted anchor outward and inverts parent_of; superscripts match positions; the child groups tile the iterated family.

tests.name: test_the_two_families_are_never_mixed
tests.what: homotopy_name vs name read the same ElementRef value differently per family, and out-of-family refs raise KeyError / are not 'in' naming.
tests.concern: Good guard of the 'ElementRef carries no family tag' rule.

tests.name: test_homotopy_only_naming_is_its_own_parent
tests.what: ElementNaming(homotopy) alone treats each element as its own parent/child, unsplit; describe() contains the exact line 'L_(0.0;2)  (#1)'.
tests.concern: describe() substring with exact double-space formatting is a cosmetic pin.

tests.name: test_branch_codes_always_and_letters_only_with_two_fixed_points
tests.what: Branch codes always appear; letters only when the family spans two fixed points (A:/B:), short-form lookup is ambiguous across branches, branch_code strings, tag prefixes ElementRef.label, describe mentions '2 lettered fixed points'.
tests.concern: Encodes the 2026-09-30 author naming rule (legit) but packs many exact strings including a describe() phrase; the position-letter fallback (A, B by order) is pinned implicitly.

tests.name: test_fixed_point_label_wins_over_position_and_disambiguates_ref_labels
tests.what: FixedPoint.label overrides positional letters in names, and ElementRef.label strings differ for same-period saddles ('Q:p1@0.0/L#0').
tests.concern: Exact ElementRef.label format pinned; the important bit is that the two labels differ.

tests.name: test_missing_parent_id_reads_as_own_parent
tests.what: Iterated intervals with parent_element_id=None are treated as their own (same-id) parent.
tests.concern: Defensive fallback behaviour; may be an implementation choice rather than a rule (real iterated partitions always set parents).
tests.question: Should an iterated element without parent_element_id silently become its own parent, or should that be an error?

tests.name: test_bad_parent_raises_value_error
tests.what: A nonexistent parent id or a side missing from the homotopy family raises ValueError with specific messages.
tests.concern: match= strings pin message wording.

tests.name: test_names_are_deterministic_across_builds
tests.what: Two ElementNaming builds from the same families produce identical names, refs and describe().
tests.concern: Weak: building twice from the SAME objects in-process is nearly tautological for a deterministic constructor (would only catch set-iteration nondeterminism across runs, which this cannot detect).

tests.name: test_k10_homotopy_names
tests.what: The k=10 homotopy family is exactly {L_1..L_3, R_1..R_3} with no letters.
tests.concern: Raw k=10 fixture fact (3 elements per side); subsumed by test_k10_iterated_names which implies the parents.

tests.name: test_k10_iterated_names
tests.what: The k=10 iterated family is exactly the 11 names L_1^1,L_1^2,L_2,L_3,R_1^1..R_1^3,R_2,R_3^1..R_3^3 with the stated parent/children groups.
tests.concern: Pins the k=10 iterated cut outcome, which depends on the empty-stretch cut rule (changed 09-21 and 09-23) and the fixture's growth depth; it is a documented CLAUDE.md fixture fact, but it is the same fact as test_dual_graph's K10_ITERATED_NAMES and the names asserted in test_symbolic_dynamics. This really tests PartitionFamily's cut, not ElementNaming.
tests.question: Should the k=10 iterated-element layout be pinned once in a single 'fixture facts' file rather than in naming, dual-graph and symbolic tests?

tests.name: test_k10_names_agree_with_the_partition_structure
tests.what: On k=10, every iterated element's name agrees with its interval's parent_element_id/side, round-trips via ref_of/lookup, and every child lies within its parent's cdist span.
tests.concern: Good structural invariant independent of exact fixture facts; the child-within-parent check is really a PartitionFamily invariant.

tests.name: test_k10_describe_lists_every_parent_with_its_children
tests.what: k=10 describe() contains exact lines like 'R_(0.0;1)  (#0) -> R_(0.0;1)^1, R_(0.0;1)^2, R_(0.0;1)^3' and '11 iterated element(s)'.
tests.concern: Pins a human-readable report's exact formatting AND a fixture fact (11 elements) at once; double failure surface for no scientific value beyond test_k10_iterated_names.

tests.name: test_p3_names_carry_branch_codes_and_letters
tests.what: With the nested period-3 + period-1 fixture partitioned, letters map each fixed point to its label, distinct codes per branch key, every name text/ref label starts with the letter, and round-trips hold.
tests.concern: Marked slow; largely duplicates tests/test_higher_period_cartoon.py::test_nested_names_carry_fixed_point_letters (same letter rule on the nested build) and the synthetic two-fixed-point test.

result.shard_summary: This shard covers 53 tests (34 in test_dual_walk.py, 19 in test_element_naming.py). Together they run in about 0.7s, so cost is not a problem; the k10/p3 fixtures take about 0.1s each. test_dual_walk.py is mostly well-designed synthetic algorithm-contract testing. It builds FakeDual graphs and hand-made partition families to check the walk spec in CLAUDE.md: entry-then-exit recording, walls never crossed, merged-face skip, shortest layer only, ambiguity, dedupe, max_walks truncation and determinism. It does the same for land_element (table first, per_step_beta scaling, orientation flip, singleton, straddle) and for trellis_itinerary (the row rule and direction -1 reversal). The main overtesting pattern there is string coupling. About ten tests also assert log-message substrings, reason strings or repr text ('faces 2 faces', 'NON-singleton'/'backward only', 'straddles', 'instead of', '1 step(s)'). These duplicate the status/resolved fields that already carry the contract. A few small tests are near-duplicates that could be parametrized (the two trivial cases, the left/right crossing mirror, the three table-landing cases). The single k=10 integration test largely duplicates test_symbolic_dynamics' k=10 tests. test_element_naming.py tests the documented naming rules well: anchor-outward subscripts, parent-grouped superscripts, the family-separation rule, round trips, and letters only with several fixed points. However, it pins the 2026-09-30 notation as exact strings (text, mathtext, repr, ElementRef.label, describe() lines with exact double spaces) in many places. The k=10 iterated-name set (11 names) is a cut-rule fixture fact that is also pinned in test_dual_graph and test_symbolic_dynamics. The describe() and repr tests, and the 'deterministic across builds' test (which is close to tautological), are the clearest candidates to delete. No test here asserts a superseded rule. One test (singleton owned by a non-singleton) leans on the backward-only-holes rule, whose period-k exemption is PROVISIONAL, but it pins only the period-1 consequence.
gaps: shortest_walks with several fixed points / cross-branch unified nodes (only the trivial fixed_points=[key[0]] pass-through is tested); walks crossing between stable branches of a period-k orbit are untested synthetically
land_element on a period-k key where advance_key changes orbit index / flips branch with inversion (all synthetic landings use a single branch whose image is itself)
land_element with orientation_preserving=False combined with a singleton or straddle case
trellis_itinerary with equal consecutive crossing signs (the case where rows come out opposite and a cross-side pair should be flagged)
No synthetic test that a unified node exists only on the strong pip's fundamental segment (that is in test_dual_graph presumably, not here)
ElementNaming lookup of short form when only one branch exists but two fixed points (letter required?) and the mathtext of an unsplit lettered name

tests.name: test_odd_noise_run_keeps_median_and_purges_rest
tests.what: Three crossings within ~1e-12 relative unstable cdist collapse to the median; a 1e-3-separated crossing survives; discarded pairs leave _intersecting_segments.
tests.concern: Private method with hand-crafted numbers copied from an observed blast; the odd/even parity heuristic is a numerics design choice the author may revise. Keeping the median (vs. any one) is a specific choice.

tests.name: test_even_noise_run_is_a_grazing_artifact_and_drops
tests.what: Two near-identical detections are treated as a grazing artifact and both dropped.
tests.concern: Pins the parity rule (even run = no crossing); scientifically reasonable for transversal noise but could drop a real tangential pair -- a heuristic, not a law.
tests.question: Is the parity rule (odd noise run keeps its median, even run drops entirely) a settled rule you want enforced, or a heuristic that may change?

tests.name: test_genuinely_separate_crossings_are_untouched
tests.what: Crossings with ~1e-3 relative gaps are all kept and their segment pairs remain.

tests.name: test_period3_unstable_manifolds_do_not_self_cross
tests.what: Within |x|,|y|<6, no unstable manifold of the p3 session transversally crosses ITSELF (O(n^2) brute force).
tests.concern: Docstring and file name promise 'two unstable curves never cross' but only self-crossings per manifold are checked: unstable-vs-unstable across branches/fixed points and stable-vs-stable are untested. Only the p3 fixture. The 6.0 window and 1e-15/1e-9 thresholds are ad hoc.

result.shard_summary: This shard (47 tests, 7 files, ~1.1k lines) covers the crossing/segment layer: BridgeId identity and the derived image/preimage genealogy (test_bridge_identity), Intersection/IntersectionRegistry small fixes, the Tangle segment index and scale-invariant crossing predicates, Point insertion side effects, cdist interpolation, noise-crossing collapse, and an unstable no-self-crossing check. The whole shard runs in 3.4s (slowest 1.3s, the inversion saddle), so cost is not an issue; the `slow` markers on the henon_p3_session tests do not match measured time (~0.1-0.2s setup), which suggests that fixture is cached or the marker is stale. Strengths: the genealogy tests use independent oracles (the bridges_at chain walk for preimage_bridges), the geometry-kernel tests are exact synthetic configurations, and the noise-collapse tests are pure unit tests. Overtesting patterns: (1) many assertions go through private Tangle dicts (_manifold_segs, _seg_lookup, _seg_manifolds, _intersecting_segments) and private workbench containers (_bridges, _partial_bridges), so a rewrite of the index would break them while behaviour stayed correct; (2) negative hasattr pins of finished refactors (deleted genealogy attributes); (3) a raw fixture count (small_tangle has exactly 2 crossings); (4) an exact DEBUG log substring; (5) private _get_lambda_u tests for on_interval, which has no caller in src/, uses the full lambda instead of per_step_beta, and pins a cross-saddle eigenvalue fallback that is scientifically dubious; (6) same invariant duplicated per fixture (k=10 vs p3) instead of parametrized, and duplicates of test_single_source_of_truth (id ordering, partial bridges, unstable-segment cdist bracket). Under-testing: the fundamental invariant is checked only weakly. The 'no same-stability crossing' test checks only unstable SELF-crossings on one fixture, and the one-unstable-one-stable check runs only on the tiny k=10 fixture's private index. The inversion test's docstring calls the per-branch-pair anchors a defect, which conflicts with CLAUDE.md's current design.
gaps: Unstable-vs-unstable crossings between DIFFERENT branches or fixed points (e.g. nested p1+p3) are never checked; the file named test_no_same_stability_crossing only counts self-crossings per manifold.
No stable-vs-stable (or stable self-crossing) geometric check at all.

The registry-level form of the fundamental invariant (every registered crossing has an unstable manifold_a_key and a stable manifold_b_key) is not asserted on the period-3, nested or blasted fixtures, where same-stability artifacts actually appear.
Nothing checks that same-stability pairs are discarded AND logged during compute_intersections (CLAUDE.md says they are worth logging), e.g. with a synthetic u x u near-tangent pair.
preserve_ids=True keeping registry ids stable across compute_intersections is only covered indirectly through the iterated flag, not by comparing ids/cdists before and after.
_collapse_noise_crossings is tested only in isolation; no end-to-end test shows a deep blast producing no duplicate crossings or clone bridges.

Bridge cutting at exact registry crossings (bridge endpoints exactly equal to registry coords) is not asserted in this shard; it lives only in the exact-value fingerprint pins of test_single_source_of_truth.
on_interval / iterate-cdist scaling for period > 1 (per_step_beta vs lambda) is untested, and the existing helper does not match the CLAUDE.md per-step rule.

result.shard_summary: tests/test_topology_plotting.py holds 45 test functions (65 collected items with parametrization) and runs in about 4 s. Every test is fast: k10_partitioned and the local henon_session cost roughly 0.05-0.15 s each to set up. The file mixes four unrelated concerns. (1) Leftovers from the "Phase 8" refactor that check module layout: plotters live in plotting.py, StablePartition has no plt, Trellis has no _HOLE_* attributes, Trellis methods delegate through a mock, and session fan-outs go through the private _fanout_plot/_fanout_call (10 parametrized mock tests). These are implementation-detail pins with almost no behavioural value, and they are the clearest candidates for deletion. (2) verbose/logging contract tests. They are legitimate but are not plotting, so they belong in a logging or Trellis suite. (3) Real plotting behaviour on the k=10 fixture: dual-graph node geometry (side placement, face points inside regions, the copy regression), walks, bridges-by-class, transition graph, itinerary table and the dual-graph cartoon layout (ordinal ranks, brackets matching closedness, one node per element, bridges and walks drawn element to element). The geometric and count checks here are good. The main overtesting is exact pins of legend wording, title strings, label separators, ha/va alignment, marker face colours, palette slot order, the order of artists in ax.collections, a re-implemented clip-padding formula, and layout heuristics that depend on fonts and DPI. Examples of the last are the itinerary column being the widest, a 60 pt row height at 5% tolerance, and a font-shrink floor of 4. (4) Several k=10 fixture facts that are owned elsewhere. The k=10 right-row closedness [ ] ( ) ... is duplicated verbatim from test_iterated_partition.py. Other repeated facts: u is inert, a self-loop exists, walks_drawn==1, and the inert itinerary string 'L_(0.0;1)^1 L_(0.0;1)^1'. test_plot_itinerary_table_lists_every_class is overloaded with about 10 behaviours and should be split and loosened. The local henon_session fixture re-implements the k=10 session already provided in conftest (k10_session). Two tests fabricate states that the fixture never produces: they mutate names or member_refinement. These test defensive branches, and the author should confirm those branches matter.
gaps: plot_strong_pip_candidates / plot_strong_pip / plot_pseudoneighbors / plot_holes / plot_stable_partition default output is only smoke-tested (non-None); no check that holes use HOLE_MARKERS/HOLE_COLORS per orbit or that pseudoneighbor pairs are all drawn
plot_dual_graph face-to-node edges are never counted against dg.graph() edges
Transition-graph virtual sinks (dashed) are never exercised: k=10 has no virtual class
plot_bridges_by_class with a real unmatched member is never exercised, and color_bridges=True on the cartoon is not tested here
Cartoon inert-class dashed bridges and trellis-resolved (dotted) itineraries are never exercised on the k=10 fixture; the k=2.8 one-blast singleton/trellis path has no plotting test in this file
Itinerary table rows with 'ambiguous' or 'unresolved: ...' status are never rendered
anchor='left' drawing (only the layout mirror is checked, not the drawn artists)
Multi-tangle palettes (TANGLE_COLOR_FAMILIES, HETEROCLINIC_COLORS) and branch-code/fixed-point-letter names in plots are not covered here (partly covered in test_higher_period_cartoon.py)
plot_minimal_trellis hole vs image styling (thick/thin) is not distinguished, only line counts

result.shard_summary: These three files cover 57 tests: ElementRef identity, the combinatorial row (row_of_end) and BridgeClass/BridgeClassTable construction (test_bridge_class.py, 30), the TangleSession.bridge_classes facade with its caching, BridgeAlphabet letters and resonance-zone annotation (test_session_bridge_classes.py, 19), and the MinimalTrellis (test_minimal_trellis.py, 8). Cost is low: fixtures build in 0.05 to 0.3 s and the whole shard runs in about 9 s. Only two tests cost real time: the bespoke 10-step zone test (2.4 s) and the growth-based cache-invalidation test (1.6 s). Several p3 tests are marked @slow but are cheap. The main strengths are a few tests that check real science: row_of_end checked against the geometric _row_at on two fixtures, a hand-built unit test of the 2026-09-16 inertness fixed point (_resolve_inertness) that needs no fixture, the dense _check_minimal battery, and the k=2.8 virtual-loop inertness test. There are four overtesting patterns. (1) The k=10 class picture (2 classes, 4 active members, one folded loop, unresolved inert member, letter 'a') is re-asserted in about 6 tests across both files, plus in the slow zone test. (2) Four tests assert exact describe()/report wording or log substrings. (3) There are duplicates: the p3 "no class mixes fixed points" check appears near-verbatim in both files; the session-vs-direct checks overlap with the private _gathered_partitions check; the cache-hit/invalidation/read tests repeat the same pattern used in the dual-graph, symbolic-dynamics and trellis-cache files. (4) Some tests check implementation details: an identity check that image_chain is _image_chain, the private session._bridge_classes dict size, and private Arrangement internals inside _check_minimal. Two tests encode the SUPERSEDED pre-2026-09-30 ordering. test_direction_matches_the_element_order_at_the_ends asserts element_sort_key(source) <= element_sort_key(target), and test_classes_and_members_come_out_in_the_documented_order re-implements the sort without the tangle grouping. Both pass only because k=10 has one branch and one tangle. They should be rewritten against anchor_outward_key and the tangle-grouped order. test_minimal_trellis.py's docstring still says inertness "is changing on a concurrent branch", which has been stale since 2026-09-16.
gaps: Cross-branch anchor-outward orientation (2026-09-30, anchor_outward_key: smaller element_id first across branches) is never tested; a hand-built two-branch ElementRef pair through oriented_class would cover it with no fixture.

Tangle grouping of the table (entry.tangle, connecting classes last, tangle=None for a class connecting two tangles) is tested in this shard only on a one-tangle fixture. Only test_higher_period_cartoon checks grouping, and nothing checks a connecting/heteroclinic class at all.
Loop folding through a multi-step preimage chain (a loop whose immediate preimage is itself a loop) is not exercised.
Inertness through a class mapping to an inert class on a real fixture (propagation, not just the hand-built table) is not tested on a trellis.

No test checks the minimal trellis on a period-k orbit where an image chain crosses onto another orbit branch, or that a subdivided image contributes every consecutive pair on a real fixture (k=2.8 two blasts is not used here).
The minimal trellis's 'outermost crossing per stable branch' and 'anchors' kept-node rule is re-derived inside _check_minimal rather than stated as an independent expectation.
The zone annotation for a class with members in no zone versus straddling zones is only tested by monkeypatching classify_bridge; there is no real two-zone fixture.

tests.name: test_every_detected_crossing_has_a_definite_sign
tests.what: Every registered crossing (anchors included) has crossing_sign in {+1,-1}.
tests.concern: Mostly implied by the cross-product test below (which also covers non-synthetic crossings); this one adds only the anchors and the no-zero guarantee.

tests.name: test_crossing_sign_is_the_cross_product_of_the_two_directions
tests.what: Recomputes each non-synthetic crossing's sign from the flanking manifold nodes (increasing-cdist directions) and checks it equals the stored crossing_sign.
tests.concern: The searchsorted-on-cdist local direction could pick a neighbouring segment at a near-tangency; currently passes but is a theoretical flake source if growth changes.

tests.name: test_anchor_sign_matches_the_oriented_eigendirections
tests.what: Each synthetic anchor's crossing_sign equals the sign of the cross product of the first segments of its unstable and stable manifolds.

tests.name: test_signs_alternate_along_a_stable_branch
tests.what: On the k=10 trellis, consecutive crossings along every stable branch have opposite signs (at least 3 pairs).
tests.concern: Its own docstring says this is NOT an invariant (fails for nested / period-k / dead-ended unstable branches); it is a fixture pin used as a sentinel for a systematic sign error. Fine as a sentinel, but it belongs with fixture-sanity checks, not with arrangement contracts, and would break if the k=10 fixture is regrown differently.
tests.question: Is the cross-product test (which recomputes every sign directly) enough to catch a sign error, so this fixture-dependent alternation sentinel can go?

tests.name: test_hand_built_arrangement_has_exactly_one_closed_face
tests.what: A hand-built one-lobe trellis yields 2 faces, 1 region and 1 open face; the region is closed, has corners (a,b), both arc kinds and bridge_ids [(a,b)].

tests.name: test_hand_built_region_geometry_closes_and_contains_its_lobe
tests.what: The hand-built lobe's boundary ring has at least 3 points, contains (1,1) but not (-1,1), verifies its representative point, and has negative (clockwise) signed area.
tests.concern: area < 0 pins the clockwise traversal convention. CLAUDE.md documents that convention, so it is a legitimate pin.

tests.name: test_hand_built_lookups
tests.what: region() accepts any rotation of the corners, regions_at, regions_bounded_by and neighbor_across return the lobe or None as expected, and region((a,)) is None.

tests.name: test_every_bridge_must_be_consecutive_on_its_branch
tests.what: Corrupting a bridge's second endpoint makes Arrangement.from_trellis raise an AssertionError matching 'not consecutive crossings'.
tests.concern: Pins the assertion message text. Rewording the assertion breaks the test even though the guard still works.

tests.name: test_an_arc_without_a_bridge_is_still_an_arc
tests.what: With the bridge list emptied, the lobe still closes with corners (a,b) and no bridge_ids, and its geometry collapses to the exact chord [[0,0],[0,2]] with area exactly 0.0.
tests.concern: The combinatorial half (an arc with no bridge still closes a face) is a real contract that blasts rely on. The exact chord coordinates and area==0.0 pin a 'documented degradation' fallback, and that pin would break if the fallback improved (for example by reading the parent manifold).
tests.question: Is the chord-collapse fallback for a bridgeless arc a behaviour you want enforced, or just today's degradation that a better fallback may replace?

tests.name: test_canonical_corners_preserves_cyclic_order
tests.what: canonical_corners rotates a corner list to start at its minimum while keeping cyclic order; empty gives ().
tests.concern: A small unit test of a helper. The rotate-to-minimum choice is a convention, but region lookup depends on it.

tests.name: test_arc_reverse_round_trips
tests.what: Arc.reversed swaps tail and head, keeps edge_key, and is an involution.
tests.concern: Near-trivial dataclass test, but cheap.

tests.name: test_k10_arrangement_is_one_component_and_euler_holds
tests.what: The k=10 arrangement has 1 component, V-E+F = 2, at least 1 open face, and no containing faces.
tests.concern: V-E+F == 2*components depends on the implementation counting one outer face per component (documented). The open_faces >= components check is weak.

tests.name: test_k10_regions_are_pairwise_disjoint
tests.what: No k=10 region's representative point lies inside any other region.
tests.concern: The same check is repeated for p3; could be one parametrized invariant over both fixtures.

tests.name: test_p3_arrangement_is_two_components_and_euler_holds
tests.what: The nested period-3 + period-1 arrangement has exactly 2 components and V-E+F = 4.
tests.concern: Euler relative to component_count is invariant. 'Exactly 2 components' is a fixture fact: it holds only because no heteroclinic crossing is computed at this growth, so growing further or computing heteroclinic crossings would legitimately change it. The slow mark looks stale: the fixture setup measured about 0.15s.

tests.name: test_p3_regions_are_pairwise_disjoint
tests.what: No nested-fixture region's representative point lies inside another region (the regression guard for the outer face swallowing inner faces).
tests.concern: A duplicate of the k10 version on another fixture.

tests.name: test_p3_arrangement_regions_are_geometrically_sound

tests.concern: A duplicate of the k10 version; also prints.

tests.concern: The slowest test in the shard (0.8s, from the extra growth). It is the only arrangement-cache test; trellis and generation caching are covered in numerics/test_generation_and_caches.py. It belongs in a facade/caching file rather than with the arrangement contracts.

tests.concern: The assertions are weak: they check only a matching branch key and a side value, never which element an arc gets. It reruns the partition pipeline by hand instead of using the k10_partitioned fixture.

tests.name: test_k10_region_images_agree_with_the_dynamics
tests.what: For each k=10 region with a combinatorial image_of, mapping its representative point with the real map lands only in that image, and the image's area matches within 2%.
tests.concern: The test can pass vacuously: unlike the p3 twin, it never asserts with_image > 0, and per another docstring only one k=10 region has an image. It also prints.

tests.name: test_k10_rejects_an_image_that_is_only_a_sub_face
tests.what: On k=10, every closed face that carries a region's mapped corners is strictly smaller than the source, image_of returns None for it, and some other region has the missing area (2% tolerance); at least one such carrier exists.
tests.concern: This is the only test of the area-based sub-face rejection, but it relies on a k=10 fixture accident (exactly one region whose mapped corners land on a smaller split face). It asserts that EVERY carrier is too small, so regrowing the fixture so that some region has a genuine full-size carrier would fail it. The 'missing area equals some other region' check accepts any region of matching area.
tests.question: Would you accept replacing this fixture-dependent check with a hand-built arrangement in which an extra stable arc deliberately splits the image face?

tests.name: test_p3_region_images_agree_with_the_dynamics
tests.what: On the nested fixture, at least one region has an image, and every combinatorial image agrees with the real map and preserves area within 2%.
tests.concern: Prints.

tests.name: test_preimage_of_a_region_is_its_hand_derived_backward_image
tests.what: For nested-fixture regions whose corners have registered -1 iterates forming a same-area region, preimage_of returns that region and the real forward map sends its representative point into the source.
tests.concern: Its skip conditions are broad, but it is guarded by checked > 0.

tests.name: test_preimage_inverts_image
tests.what: For nested-fixture regions where both directions are defined, preimage_of(image_of(R)) is R, with at least one round trip.
tests.concern: Substantially overlaps the hand-derived preimage test. Both are cheap.

tests.name: test_arrangement_survives_a_blast
tests.what: After blasting the k=10 zone twice, the arrangement builds, has regions, has at least one unstable arc with no bridge_id, and every representable region verifies its representative point (collapsed ones report None and area 0).
tests.concern: A good regression guard. The 'at least one bridgeless unstable arc' assertion depends on blast internals (blast children not being cut into bridges). If blasting later creates bridges for every iterated arc, that assertion fails while the arrangement is still correct.

tests.name: test_dense_build_over_all_three_lobes_has_three_regions
tests.what: The dense arrangement over three hand-built lobes has 3 regions and Euler characteristic 2.
tests.concern: Fully covered by test_sparse_and_dense_agree_when_every_bridge_is_kept, which asserts 3 regions for dense too.

tests.name: test_sparse_unstable_arcs_are_exactly_the_kept_bridges
tests.what: In sparse mode with lobes ab and cd kept, the unstable arcs are exactly {(a,b),(c,d)}, arrangement.sparse is True, and summary() contains 'sparse'.
tests.concern: The summary-string check is a cosmetic pin.

tests.concern: This enforces the dense mode's gap-filling as behaviour. It is intended (dense arcs come from consecutive crossings), but it pins a property that is mainly there to motivate sparse mode.

tests.name: test_sparse_kept_endpoints_are_degree_three_without_unstable_stubs

tests.concern: It reads private half-edge internals and slot naming ('s+', 'u-'). Any refactor of the rotation-system representation breaks it while the faces stay identical. The observable contract (no unstable stubs, so the gap merges into the outer face) is already covered by the face, Euler and dangling-end-count tests.

tests.name: test_sparse_faces_close_and_euler_holds
tests.what: Sparse mode with two kept lobes gives 2 regions, 3 faces, 1 component, Euler 2, and region corners {a,b} and {c,d}.
tests.concern: The corner assertion is an 'A or B' where B (set comparison) subsumes A, so the first clause is dead weight.

tests.concern: Redundant: Trellis.punch_holes already runs check_holes_share_bridge_side internally (Trellis.py ~1116), so the henon_punched fixture would already have raised. The test adds only 'holes is non-empty', and p3 and deep-blast variants exist in test_stable_partition_period3.py.

tests.concern: Partly redundant, since punch_holes already checks hole-bearing bridges, but this extends the check to all bridges. It duplicates test_p3_bridge_rows_consistent on another fixture; a single parametrized invariant would be cleaner.

tests.name: test_henon_partition_still_built_after_wiring
tests.what: After punching, partition_stable_manifold on branch (fp,stable,0,0) returns results ordered ['left','right'], each with intervals.
tests.concern: A historical smoke test from when the invariant checks were wired into punch_holes. It pins the left-then-right return order and is otherwise weak: every partition test and the k10_partitioned fixture already exercise this path.

result.shard_summary: This shard has 46 tests across three files. test_arrangement.py (28) covers the crossing-sign datum, the half-edge Arrangement on a hand-built one-lobe trellis, and the k=10 and nested-p3 fixtures (Euler, region disjointness, region soundness, map-verified images and preimages with area preservation, containing faces, generation caching, post-blast robustness). test_arrangement_sparse.py (6) covers sparse versus dense mode on a hand-built three-lobe line. test_topology_invariants.py (12) covers the I1 hole-side and I2 bridge-row checks on synthetic violations and on k=10. The shard is cheap: the whole shard runs in about 3s, and even the slow-marked p3 tests have about 0.15s setup, so those marks look stale. The main strength is that most real-fixture tests are genuine invariants: they check the arrangement against the real map, area preservation and Euler, not hard-coded counts, and the synthetic fixtures make the face counts derivable by hand. Overtesting patterns: (1) k10/p3 twin tests (disjointness, soundness, image agreement, Euler) should be single parametrized invariants; (2) several tests pin formatted strings: assertion messages, summary() text such as '+2 dangling ends', and 'sparse' in summary; (3) one sparse test reads private _nodes, slots and _half_edges internals; (4) test_henon_holes_share_bridge_side is redundant because punch_holes already runs that check; (5) a few pins tie to fixture accidents: the 2 components on p3, the alternating signs on k=10, the sub-face carrier that exists only on k=10, and the chord-collapse coordinates. Weak spots: the k10 image-agreement test can pass vacuously (no with_image > 0 guard), and the neighbour block in regions_at/bounded_by is near-tautological. Nothing in this shard pins a superseded or PROVISIONAL CLAUDE.md rule; the clockwise-face convention it pins is documented.
gaps: No test of the sparse-mode arrangement on a real minimal trellis beyond test_minimal_trellis's Euler/kept-arcs check: for example, that sparse regions are pairwise disjoint and that image_of works (or is refused) in sparse mode.
The area-based sub-face rejection in image_of is only exercised through a k=10 fixture accident; there is no deterministic hand-built case.

Arrangement on a period-k or inversion fixture, where crossings of different unstable branches interleave on one stable branch, is never built. Signs need not alternate there, and the rotation-from-own-sign claim is untested.
preimage_of/image_of with n > 1 or negative n is never tested.
containing_faces is only exercised through nested p3; there is no hand-built two-component nesting test that would pin the classification without growth.

The orientation-reversing path of the row and side invariants is exercised only synthetically; no real orientation-reversing map (b < 0) appears anywhere, consistent with the conftest note that FixedPoint.set_k_value rejects it.
No arrangement test checks that the anchor (synthetic crossing at cdist (0,0)) gets correct rotation when several unstable branches share it.

tests.name: test_iterate_composes_single_steps_when_the_table_has_no_direct_entry

tests.concern: Tests Trellis, not the dual graph (misplaced 'pre-task' leftover). Hard-asserts the precondition table[q0,2] is None: if inference ever starts storing direct multi-step entries the test FAILS instead of skipping, although composition would still be correct.
